anomalies.observed: On the /Microcontroller/ sheet (mcu.kicad_sch), the USB-C receptacle J5 VBUS pin (A4) node carries the global label 'VBUS' together with the '+5V' power symbol on the same junction. On the /Power/ sheet, U8 (TPS2121RUXR) pin 2 (IN2) is on the +5V net and pin 1 (OUT) is on the VBUS net, so the two labels now denote one and the same net.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the USB VBUS pins feed the '+5V' net which drives mux IN2, while the mux output is a separate internal 'VBUS' rail: 'J12 ... VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2)' and 'note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux.' The USB supply and the mux output must not share a net.

evidence.quote: mcu.kicad_sch (sheet /Microcontroller/): J5 pin A4 wired to a junction bearing both the '+5V' power symbol and the red global label 'VBUS'
power.kicad_sch (sheet /Power/): U8 TPS2121RUXR pin 2 IN2 -> '+5V'; pin 1 OUT -> 'VBUS' (TP3)
J12 ... VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2) ... note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux

anomalies.impact: Mux input 2 (+5V) is shorted to the mux output (VBUS). When the 12 V barrel jack is present the mux passes ~12 V onto VBUS, which is now hard-wired to the USB 5 V source, so the two supplies fight through the mux's low-resistance path: USB host over-current, brown-out of the buck input, and complete loss of the seamless-switchover arbitration that U5 is there to provide.

parsed.summary: The USB-C VBUS pin (J5.A4) is labelled with the mux-output net 'VBUS' and joined to '+5V', merging the power mux's IN2 rail with its OUT rail, which contradicts the spec's requirement that +5V and VBUS be distinct nets and defeats the TPS2121 arbitration; all other traced values, pin assignments and thermocouple/SPI/heater/fan/USB connections match the specification.
